Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

High-level approach (summary):
- Run types: ramp-to-steady, sustained soak (90+ minutes), spike bursts (3x short bursts), and cold-start sweep (replica churn).
- Metrics: end-to-end request latency (server-side start -> final token emitted), token-time breakdowns, decode-time, queueing latency, kernel / GPU utilization, and per-replica KV cache hit rates. We'll include how we compute p50/p95/p99 with sample scripts.
- Model variants: we'll provide throughput curves for 7B and 13B in both fp16 and 4-bit quantized profiles; recommended replica counts per target QPS and suggested batching windows.
- Warmup policy: explicit prefix-cache warmup phase, synthetic prefix replay for short prompt workloads, and guidance on sharding KV cache when using burstable traffic.

Michael / team — attaching the numbers inline for the specific asks. Notes up front: numbers are empirical with our internal load harness using a mix of 60% short (prompt < 64 tokens) and 40% long (prompt 256–1024 tokens) payloads. Variability increases with the ratio of long decodes.

Throughput curves (representative per replica):
- 7B fp16: base batching window 8 tokens -> sustained QPS: 48; window 16 -> QPS: 72; QPS drops ~10% under mixed long-decode profile.
- 7B 4-bit quantized: same hardware -> sustained QPS: 78 (window 16), peak short-burst QPS up to 120 for <32-token prompts with aggressive batching.
- 13B fp16: window 8 -> QPS: 22; window 16 -> QPS: 34; under mixed workload expect ~20% variance.
- 13B 4-bit quantized: window 16 -> QPS: 48; warmup penalties worse on 13B when KV cache cold.

Autoscaling guidance:
- Primary signal: 95th percentile queueing latency per replica > 25ms for >30s -> add replica.
- Secondary signal: GPU util > 70% and average batch size > 75% of configured window -> add replica.
- Downscale: sustained 95th queueing < 10ms and GPU util < 35% for 90s.

Warmup & cache policy:
- Warmup phase: synthetic replay of the last 24 hours of unique prefixes at 50–80% of target concurrency for 20–30 minutes.
- Cold-start accounting: report both cold-start p95/p99 and steady-state p95/p99; include a flag in logs (cache_state=warm/cold) so traces can be filtered.

Lab artifacts to collect (short list):
- per-request: request_id, start_ts, first_byte_ts, last_token_ts, total_token_count, model_variant, replica_id, cache_state
- per-replica: GPU_util, decode_ms_per_token, kernel_queue_depth, model_mem_pages

I'll drop an Excel sheet (redwood_latency_throughput_runbook.xlsx) with the curves and the sample scripts for computing pN.

— Vivek
Principal Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference

Lisa — attaching the completed runbook and a short checklist for your SREs (see attachments). Highlights and what you'll see inside: 

1) Test phases (exact sequence):
   - Phase A: KV/Prefix warmup (20–30m) — script provided to replay prefixes.
   - Phase B: Ramp (10m linear to target concurrency).
   - Phase C: Steady-state soak (60–120m depending on acceptance criteria).
   - Phase D: Spike bursts (3 x 30s bursts at 2–3x concurrency separated by 5m).
   - Phase E: Cold-start sweep (simulate replica churn, measure cold p95/p99).

2) Metrics (exact metric names):
   - redwood.request.latency.total_ms (server start -> last token)
   - redwood.request.latency.first_byte_ms
   - redwood.token.decode_ms_per_token
   - redwood.replica.queueing_ms_p95
   - redwood.cache.kv_hit_rate

3) Mapping guidance: QPS per replica for 7B/13B across quantization profiles (see sheet). Includes 95% CI and notes about uncertainty under very long-decode workloads.

4) Autoscaling recipe: primary & secondary triggers with hysteresis windows and a suggested fallback policy to degrade to the 7B quantized model when tail latency breaches SLA.

5) Artifacts & upload checklist: trace ids CSV, GPU counters, sample request payloads (anonymized), and the run summary.

Attachments: acme_perf_questionnaire_v2.pdf (filled), redwood_latency_throughput_runbook.xlsx, lab-test-checklist.txt

If you want, we can do a 30m walkthrough with your SREs tomorrow to step through the scripts. Let me know a time and we'll send a calendar invite.
